# 2B.4 Research Note: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in 2024

Bottom line: the 2024 record is **mostly negative** on civilian protection and proportionality in military operations. I found direct reporting on Turkish operations in **Syria/Iraq** and Turkey-linked drone strikes in **Somalia** that allege civilian harm, abusive detention, and proxy abuses. I did **not** find reliable 2024 operational evidence showing Erdoğan publicly improved IHL compliance or prisoner treatment.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Cuts against 2B.4 | [World Report 2024: Türkiye](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/turkey) | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/turkey | HRW says Türkiye intensified its military campaign against the PKK with drone strikes in northern Iraq and northeast Syria; October strikes damaged critical infrastructure and disrupted water and electricity for millions. This is strong evidence against proportionality/civilian-protection discipline in military operations. | `2B.4` |
| Cuts against 2B.4 | [Syria: Abuse, impunity in Turkish-occupied territories](https://www.hrw.org/tr/news/2024/02/29/syria-abuses-impunity-turkish-occupied-territories) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-02-29 | https://www.hrw.org/tr/news/2024/02/29/syria-abuses-impunity-turkish-occupied-territories | HRW says Turkey directly controls the Syrian National Army through weapons, salaries, training, and logistics, while SNA groups and military police arbitrarily detained, forcibly disappeared, tortured, and sexually abused civilians, including women and children. This is direct negative evidence on prisoner treatment and civilian protection. | `2B.4` |
| Cuts against 2B.4 | [Somalia: Death of 23 civilians in military strikes with Turkish drones may amount to war crimes – new investigation](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/somalia-death-of-23-civilians-in-military-strikes-with-turkish-drones-may-amount-to-war-crimes-new-investigation/) | Amnesty International | 2024-05-07 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/somalia-death-of-23-civilians-in-military-strikes-with-turkish-drones-may-amount-to-war-crimes-new-investigation/ | Amnesty says Somali strikes supported by Turkish drones killed 23 civilians, including 14 children, and may amount to war crimes. This is direct evidence against civilian protection and proportionality in Turkey-linked operations. | `2B.4` |
| Indirect / weakly supportive | [Türkiye President - Recep Tayyip Erdoğan - Statement summary (excerpts on the situation in oPT) - UN General Assembly - 79th Session](https://www.un.org/unispal/document/turkiye-president-recep-tayyip-unga-79-24sep24/) | UN / UNISPAL | 2024-09-24 | https://www.un.org/unispal/document/turkiye-president-recep-tayyip-unga-79-24sep24/ | Erdoğan’s public rhetoric emphasized ceasefire, humanitarian catastrophe, and stopping escalation in Gaza. This is not military-operations evidence, but it is the closest 2024 material I found that points toward civilian-protection concerns. | `2B.4`, `1B.8` |

## Search gap

I searched directly for 2024 evidence on:
- civilian protection and proportionality,
- prisoner treatment,
- IHL / humanitarian-law compliance,
- Turkish military operations in Syria, Iraq, and externally supported operations.

I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence showing Erdoğan or his government:
- publicly adopted stronger IHL safeguards,
- improved prisoner-treatment standards,
- or clearly constrained military operations on civilian-protection grounds.

So the best-supported reading is **negative overall**, with the strongest direct evidence coming from **Turkey’s Syria/Iraq campaign**, **proxy abuses in Turkish-occupied areas**, and **Turkey-linked drone strikes in Somalia**.
